title: Task-scoped escalation asking replaces session-start asking
context: Session-start orientation was asking every pending escalation, incurring one model turn per Hunch run. This imposed a fixed cost regardless of whether escalations were relevant to the actual work. Touches invariant(s): con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Escalations are now asked only for the task being worked on (matched by id/topic, prompt paths, related files, policy scope, or task selection context). Session-start asks only if the provider doesn't deliver prompt events; otherwise, the prompt hook asks task-scoped escalations once per session. All entries remain discoverable via `hunch escalations` but aren't surfaced unsolicited.
consequences: Estimated cost ratio drops 0.03–0.12 per session, wall-clock time 0.06–0.12 (measured over Codex PILOT5 runs).
Escalations become visible only when the task touches them, reducing cognitive overhead for unrelated work.
Providers without prompt-delivery capability retain session-start asking for backwards compatibility.
Agent-facing guidance stops recommending recording after routine choices; only human-decided or human-corrected items get recorded (improving signal quality in commit synthesis).
alternatives_rejected: Ask all escalations every turn (higher cost than session-start).
Disable escalation asking entirely (loses visibility into decision items).
Filter escalations in presentation only (doesn't reduce model cost or improve relevance).
Use heuristics to predict task-relevance at session start (introduces false positives/negatives).
